text:
tara_m: Quick sync — running a 30m workshop at 2pm PT to lock the competitive messaging and benchmark narrative for next week's webinar. Need final battlecard hooks + inbound routing snippet. Can folks skim the numbers?

josh_g: I can join. Are we framing vs cloud AI platforms on cost/latency or vs infra vendors on ops/control?

ana_c: leaning hard into predictable economics + graceful degradation. Customers care about 'what happens at scale' more than peak throughput. Proposed soundbite: "Predictable latency, predictable cost — even under bursty traffic."

devon_s: +1. For sales we should have 3 quick rebuttals: 1) fallback policies when capacity is constrained, 2) cost controls (batching/quantization recs), 3) private deployment story for regulated customers. Short bullets only.

sam_e: Bench numbers are uploaded — summary: p50 similar to VendorA, p90 ~1.8x lower than VendorA in bursty scenario, token cost ~0.65x with our batching & KV cache. Full CSV: https://redwood-internal.s3/bench/2845.csv (benchbot posted).

benchbot: benchmark results posted for model family alpha-2, dataset: enterprise-chat-50k. Artifacts: logs + perf traces.

ana_c: I'm drafting the benchmark narrative: emphasize methodology, steady-state vs burst, what we control (routing, cache), and what customers can expect. Will add a short section: "how we measured fallback".

josh_g: For the webinar slide we want one punchy claim + small caveat. Proposed claim: "1.8x lower p90 under realistic burst patterns — with production-safe fallbacks." Caveat line: "results vary by model/config; see notes."

devon_s: inbound routing rules — suggest simple tiering so SDRs get high-intent: 
```yaml
routing: 
  - condition: signal.score >= 0.85 and signal.company_size >= 100 -> team: enterprise-sales
  - condition: signal.feature_interest contains "dedicated" -> team: solutions-engineering
  - default -> team: inbound-nurture
```
Keep it 3 lines for the battlecard.

tara_m: love that. Ana — can you craft 3 micro-scripts for sales that map to those routes? 1 line each. Devon — can you own the battlecard doc update and drop the routing snippet there? Sam — please attach the short bench explainer to the doc (1 paragraph). I'll shepherd webinar copy.

ana_c: On it. Drafts by 4pm PT and I'll post in the doc for review. :thumbsup: 

devon_s: I'll update the battlecard at https://confluence.redwood/battlecards/competitive-signals today and ping when done.

sam_e: Attached the perf explainer in the doc now. Also added a small table of env configs used.

josh_g: I'll run a quick A/B test on two subject lines for the webinar invite tomorrow morning.

tara_m: Perfect — final checklist before 2pm:
- Ana posts 3 micro-scripts (by 4pm)
- Devon updates battlecard + routing (end of day)
- Sam attaches bench explainer (done)
- Josh sets up A/B for subject lines (tomorrow am)
If anyone can't make 2pm ping here and we can record.

benchbot: recording of perf traces will be retained for 30 days.

devon_s: FYI — I added a short one-liner vs "VendorX" for the battlecard: "Fallback + predictable unit economics vs unmanaged endpoints." Ping if we should soften language.

tara_m: Keep it pointed but factual. No jabs; focus on outcomes. See you at 2pm. :rocket:
